evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Discussion and Implications, block B0087, beginning "The bounded contribution is a project-specific synthesis", names certificate methods, proof-carrying computation, and replay-oriented workflow design as the comparison classes and disclaims novelty for those components in isolation.

text: Revised manuscript, Acknowledged Limitations, block B0091, beginning "No separately authorized field-wide novelty analysis", limits the contribution to the project-specific synthesis and prospective specification and rejects a field-wide priority claim.
items.change_summary: Relative to original blocks B0087 and B0091, the revision replaces an unsupported methodological-usefulness statement and an unpositioned-contribution admission with a named comparison-class boundary, a distinct project-specific synthesis unit, and an explicit no-global-priority limitation.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Executed Methodology, blocks B0048-B0049, replaces numbered internal phases with corpus scope, screening, evidence coding, synthesis, review, and evidentiary-limit descriptions in reader-facing scholarly terms.

text: Revised manuscript, Reproducibility and Prospective Implementation Interface, block B0080, states "Other internal workflow files are provenance surfaces, not an independently replayable scientific package."
items.change_summary: Relative to original blocks B0048-B0049 and B0080, the revision removes the Phase 2 through Phase 6 narration, states the evidence-synthesis method in corpus and coding terms, and separates retained internal workflow material as provenance.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Reproducibility and Prospective Implementation Interface, block B0080, gives a commit-pinned repository locator, four exact artifact paths, four SHA-256 digests, and the bounded claim roles those files support.

text: Revised manuscript, Data and Materials Availability, block B0107, states that the four digest-named files are available at the commit-pinned path and limits them to the bounded evidence-synthesis claims while listing unavailable evidence.
items.change_summary: Relative to the original generic artifact list and vague availability statement in B0080 and B0107, the revision supplies a commit-pinned locator, file-level digests, availability language, explicit claim-surface roles, and a narrowed auditability boundary.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Executed Methodology, block B0048, states that the evidence files preserve queried interfaces, run dates, exact query strings, normalization and deduplication rules, admitted identifiers, and source-role coding, but not row-level identifiers and decisions for every screened-out manifestation.

text: Revised manuscript, Reproducibility and Prospective Implementation Interface, block B0080, supplies separate SHA-256 digests for the source inventory and literature matrix and limits their supported uses.

text: Revised manuscript, Acknowledged Limitations, block B0089, states that the original search cannot be independently replayed record by record because screened-out row decisions and a complete external-interface run log are absent.
items.change_summary: Relative to original blocks B0048, B0089, and B0107, the revision discloses exact-query, normalization, deduplication, admitted-identifier, and artifact-digest information while expressly retaining the absence of screened-out row decisions and complete record-by-record replay.

residual_gap.text: A disclosed row-level ledger for all screened manifestations is still absent: B0048 and B0089 expressly say the screened-out row identifiers and inclusion or exclusion decisions are unavailable, and the separate inventory and matrix file digests do not hash-link the ordered 22 admitted identifiers to their evidence-matrix rows.

evidence_anchor: equation: Revised manuscript, Ideal arithmetic, block B0046, states M(h gamma h^{-1}) = M(gamma), M(gamma^{-1}) = M(gamma), and the contrasting Gaussian-conjugation relation M(gamma^{-1}) = conjugate(M(gamma)).
text: Revised manuscript, Gate M, block B0058, binds the conjugacy and inversion equations to the frozen owner relation and scopes any failure to the exact registered formula.

text: Revised manuscript, Gate M, block B0059, limits every terminal outcome to the exact registered candidate under the frozen frame and expressly rejects a conclusion about all mechanisms or codomains.
items.change_summary: Relative to original blocks B0046, B0058, and B0059, the revision adds exact conjugacy and inversion equations, defines the split-conjugate failure predicate and frozen candidate scope, and expressly blocks universal nonexistence inference.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Introduction, inserted block B0112 headed "Reader map", maps input rows through Gate Q to oriented classes and owners, maps owners and a candidate registry through Gate M to a literal ideal or typed stop receipt, restricts performance-ledger construction, and marks every node prospective.
items.change_summary: Relative to the original manuscript, the revision inserts one reader-facing dependency paragraph after B0017 that supplies object types, gate sequencing, prospective status, and a blanket prohibition on downstream use after a missing or failed node.

residual_gap.text: The single Reader map does not map a stop state to every named object or transformation: Gate Q and the performance ledger have no terminal state in that surface, and Gate M is represented only by the generic phrase "typed stop receipt" rather than its mapped stop outcomes.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Performance firewall, inserted block B0113 headed "Prospective control interpretation", maps owner-label permutation, inversion-paired, and broadened-codomain controls to diagnostic and non-diagnostic conclusions and states that no control has been run.
items.change_summary: Relative to the original manuscript, the revision inserts a control-interpretation paragraph after B0073 that gives each named control a diagnostic use, a prohibited conclusion, and an explicit unexecuted status.

residual_gap.text: The new control paragraph states what each failure diagnoses and cannot establish, but it assigns no stop state produced by failure for the owner-label permutation, inversion-paired control, or broadened-codomain control.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Gate M, block B0059, gives SPLIT_IDEAL_CODOMAIN_OBSTRUCTION precedence when split-branch compatibility under inversion fails and serializes formal_map_refuted=true in the same receipt, using FORMAL_MAP_REFUTED only when that predicate passes and another formal law fails.
items.change_summary: Relative to original block B0059's three potentially overlapping outcomes, the revision installs a deterministic split-branch-first precedence rule and specifies the single receipt content when split-branch and formal-law failure coincide.

evidence_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Reproducibility and Prospective Implementation Interface, block B0081, states that the fixtures are unexecuted specifications and that no usefulness result is reported.
text: Revised manuscript, Discussion and Implications, block B0087, states that practical usefulness and scientific performance remain unevaluated.

text: Revised manuscript, Discussion and Implications, unchanged block B0084, still states that "The literal codomain can be scientifically useful as a stress test" rather than limiting value to a prospective organizational benefit.
items.change_summary: Relative to original blocks B0081 and B0087, the revision adds explicit no-execution and no-usefulness-result limits without adding a synthetic fixture, while unchanged B0084 retains a scientific-usefulness statement.

residual_gap.text: No labeled synthetic fixture with a baseline and diagnostic outcome is present, and B0084 still asserts scientific usefulness as a stress test rather than limiting the remaining value claim to a prospective organizational benefit pending implementation.

new_issues.description: The revised methodology overstates the Round-1 panel provenance by calling the same-family, role-separated review "independent", although the frozen provenance expressly records that role separation does not remove correlated-error risk.
new_issues.location_anchor: text: Revised manuscript, Executed Methodology, block B0049, phrase "independently assessed from editorial, domain, methodology, and adversarial perspectives".
new_issues.competence_basis: The frozen R1 persona covers auditable research workflows and provenance, and the exact original/revised block comparison plus the frozen Round-1 provenance resolves this wording-level claim without external evidence.
new_issues.attribution_evidence: Original block B0049 described the reviews as "procedurally separated"; revised B0049 changes that characterization to "independently assessed", while the frozen Round-1 synthesis records model-family distinct=false and provider distinct=false and says role separation does not remove correlated-error risk.
new_issues.non_match_rationale: REV-EIC-2 operationalizes reader-facing method vocabulary and separation of workflow provenance from scientific method; it does not authorize or test a stronger claim that the review perspectives constitute an independent assessment, so using that off-criterion defect to alter REV-EIC-2 would be criteria drift.
